newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to try 19 for tourist, cinema attacks.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to try 19 for tourist, cinema attacks.

text.p: Egypt will put on trial 19 suspected Moslem militants on charges of bombing a busload of Austrian tourists and raking a Cairo cinema with machinegun fire in December 1993, security sources said on Saturday.
They said Attorney General Hisham Saraya had not yet set a date for the trial at the State Supreme Court.
Saraya's office also said the men killed police Colonel Ahmed Shalaan outside his home in Cairo in 1994 and that they had attempted to assassinate other key political figures.
The 19 defendants, including two juveniles, were also charged with belonging to Egypt's largest militant group, the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group).
Eight Austrians and eight Egyptians were wounded in December 1993 when a group of militants threw two bombs and fired shots at their bus near Cairo's ancient Amr ibn el-As mosque.
A few days earlier, militants had raked a cinema in the Cairo suburb of Helwan with machinegun fire just as crowds were leaving after the film, killing the policeman on guard and wounding six people.
Since 1992, the Gama'a has fought to topple the government and transform Egypt into a strict Islamic state. About 1,000 people have been killed in the political violence.

Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak has usually referred Moslem militants for trial in military courts because of their speedy proceedings but state security courts often hold trials for the Islamists as well and death sentences are common.
Egypt has so far sentenced around 70 people to death, 53 of whom have been executed. About six are on death row and 16 on the run.
